content_units: Gentle Knee Mobility Plan for Mild Osteoarthritis

This routine is designed for a   58-year-old beginner with mild knee osteoarthritis   who already walks   20 minutes daily  . The goal is to reduce pain, improve mobility, and build leg support without high joint stress.
Starter Context for This Routine
- This is   informational exercise guidance  , not a diagnosis or a substitute for medical care.
- The plan assumes pain is   mild and stable  , with no recent injury, major swelling, or doctor-imposed restrictions.
- A good rule: exercises should cause   no more than mild discomfort during the session   and should settle back to baseline within about   24 hours  .
Weekly Knee-Friendly Exercise Plan
Week   Dates   Focus   Key Sessions   Goal/Quiz
Week 1   Days 1-7   Learn form; reduce stiffness   3 strength days; 2 mobility days; daily 20-min walk   Finish sessions with pain staying mild
Week 2   Days 8-14   Build consistency   3 strength days; 2 mobility days; 1 optional balance add-on   Add 1-2 reps if comfortable
Week 3   Days 15-21   Improve control   3 strength days; 2 mobility days; 2 balance blocks   Move more smoothly sit-to-stand
Week 4   Days 22-28   Gentle progression   3 strength days; 2 mobility days; daily walk stays easy-moderate   Notice easier walking/stairs
Strength Days: 20-25 minutes, 3 days/week
Do these on   Monday, Wednesday, Friday   or any nonconsecutive days.
-   Warm-up, 3-5 min
- Easy marching in place
- Gentle knee bends holding a counter
- Ankle pumps
-   1. Sit-to-stand from chair   — 2 sets of 6-10
- Use a sturdy chair
- Stand up slowly, sit down with control
- Use hands on armrests if needed
-   2. Straight-leg raise   — 2 sets of 8 each leg
- Lie on back, one knee bent, one leg straight
- Tighten thigh and lift straight leg a few inches
-   3. Quad set   — 2 sets of 8-10, hold 5 seconds
- Sit or lie with leg straight
- Tighten front of thigh, press knee gently downward
-   4. Glute bridge   — 2 sets of 8
- Lie on back, knees bent
- Lift hips gently, pause, lower slowly
-   5. Standing hamstring curl   — 2 sets of 8 each leg
- Hold a chair
- Bend knee to bring heel backward without forcing range
-   6. Calf raise   — 2 sets of 10
- Hold support
- Rise up onto toes slowly, lower slowly
-   7. Side leg raise   — 1-2 sets of 8 each side
- Strengthens hip muscles that help unload the knee
-   Cool-down, 3 min
- Slow walk around room
- Gentle front-thigh and calf stretch, 20-30 seconds each
Mobility Days: 10-15 minutes, 2 days/week
Do these on   Tuesday and Saturday  .
-   Heel slides   — 10 reps each leg
- Lie down or sit, slowly slide heel toward body, then away
-   Seated knee extension   — 10 reps each leg
- Straighten knee, pause 1-2 seconds, lower slowly
-   Supported mini knee bends   — 8 reps
- Hold counter, bend only a little, keep pain mild
-   Gentle hamstring stretch   — 2 rounds each side
-   Calf stretch at wall   — 2 rounds each side
-   Weight shifts   — 30-60 seconds
- Shift weight side to side while holding support
Optional Balance Work: 2-3 times/week, 3-5 minutes
- Stand near a counter
-   Feet together hold   — 20-30 seconds
-   Semi-tandem stance   — 20 seconds each side
-   Single-leg stand with fingertip support   — 10-15 seconds each side if safe
Movements to Limit or Avoid
- Deep squats or deep lunges, especially if they increase pain
- Twisting on a planted knee
- Jumping, hopping, or high-impact aerobics
- Fast direction changes
- Kneeling for long periods if it aggravates symptoms
- Heavy leg exercises that cause pain to spike during or after
- “Push through the pain” training
A mild muscular effort is fine;   sharp joint pain is not the goal  .
Stop-and-Call Warning Signs
Stop exercise and contact a clinician promptly if he develops:
-   Sudden major swelling   in the knee
-   Redness, warmth, or fever
-   Locking   of the knee or inability to fully bend/straighten it
-   Buckling/giving way   that is new or worsening
-   Sharp pain   that does not settle with rest
- Pain that is   significantly worse the next day   and keeps recurring
- New calf swelling, calf pain, or unexplained shortness of breath
- Numbness, major weakness, or symptoms after a fall
Low-Cost Equipment Under $60 Total
Option 1: Loop resistance bands   Helpful for side steps, leg strengthening, gentle progression     $10-$15
Shop bands
Option 2: Long resistance band with handles   Useful for seated leg work and hip strengthening     $12-$20
Shop long band
Option 3: Yoga mat or padded exercise mat   Makes floor exercises more comfortable     $15-$25
Shop mat
Option 4: Small pillow or rolled towel   Supports knee during quad sets and comfort work     $0-$10
Towel guide
A practical budget combo:
- Loop bands:   $12
- Exercise mat:   $20
- Towel/pillow at home:   $0
- Total:   about $32
